speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Chairperson, I thank Members for their thoughtful suggestions.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We share the same vision of a more caring, inclusive and resilient Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We are now into the third year of our fight against COVID-19.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: It has been a test – not only for our healthcare systems, but also our social structures and support systems.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Hence, first and foremost, I thought to take this opportunity to express my deepest gratitude and appreciation to all our social workers, social service professionals and volunteers.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Throughout the pandemic, many of you stepped up – went the extra mile to care for and support Singaporeans in need, providing a critical line of social support in the community.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: At the same time, we also created over 5,000 jobs and skills opportunities in the social and early childhood sectors in the past year, including for persons with disabilities.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Singaporeans from all walks of life, joined hands and we rose against the biggest crisis of our generation.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We saw families and individuals supporting one another.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Corporates and community organisations stepping up, joining hands with the Government.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This spirit of working together has helped and enabled us to overcome crisis after crisis – from our Independence till today.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Several Members have asked about the Government's plans to uplift the low-income in Singapore – Mr Leon Perera, Mr Seah Kian Peng and Ms Ng Ling Ling.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: It begins with Singapore's Social Compact, which Minister Lawrence Wong explained in the Budget speech.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The Government creates conditions for growth and an enabling environment that provides affordable and quality education, healthcare and housing for all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Individuals work hard, doing the best for themselves and their families and this brings us dignity.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Family members support one another through the ups and downs in life – our first line of support.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Together, with the support of a caring community, the Government provides an extra hand to uplift Singaporeans in need – the low-income, the vulnerable and persons with disabilities; the citizens that MSF cares for, among others.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Social mobility becomes possible even if inequality is unavoidable.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: But we must remember that in Singapore's early days, housing, education and healthcare were nowhere near what we have today, not in terms of accessibility and much less in terms of quality.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: As a young nation, Singapore did not have much.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: But our pioneer leaders had the wisdom to prioritise education, housing and healthcare as the foundations of our Social Compact, alongside the CPF system for all Singaporeans – with discipline, decade after decade.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Equally important, the Government successfully attracted investments into Singapore, creating job opportunities.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Our forefathers worked hard because they took pride in being able to provide for their families in those hard times.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Family members, in turn, helped one another, because social assistance was very basic and reserved for the neediest.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Just like the present crisis, everyone stepped up.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Individuals, families, communities and the Government, all working together, hand in hand.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Our Social Compact remains relevant, but has evolved over the years.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: By the early 1990s, we introduced schemes like Edusave and MediFund that benefit many Singaporeans today.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We invested heavily in our preschools, schools and higher education system to give every Singaporean child the opportunities to succeed.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This has proven to be one of the biggest enablers of our society.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Through education, we enable Singaporeans to be self-reliant, as they gain skills and employment.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: And this, in turn, supports the building of assets, like housing and savings through the CPF, enabling them to care and provide for their families with dignity and, eventually, in retirement.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Low- and middle-income households continue to receive more benefits relative to taxes paid.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Today, around nine in 10 own their own homes.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Even among the low-income, home ownership remains high.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Our public healthcare system provides affordable, quality medical treatment for every citizen and is well-recognised internationally.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: An educated and trainable workforce has continued attracting investments.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Wages have grown, even after accounting for inflation, while many other advanced economies struggle with wage stagnation.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Intergenerational mobility in Singapore is higher than that in North America and Europe, including for younger cohorts born from 1985 to 1989.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Major shifts in policy have always been accompanied by efforts to enhance social assistance.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Already, more is being done to protect Singaporeans against the rapid disruptions across economies.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We must not allow inequality to be entrenched, as seen in many advanced economies.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Going forward, addressing social needs will become even more complex.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We did this over a decade ago when globalisation struck the world full-blown.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Recently, we announced the expansion of the Progressive Wage Model to uplift more low-wage workers.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: ComCare is a key component of our social safety nets.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: ComCare Short-to-Medium-Term Assistance, or SMTA, enables families to tide over temporary periods of difficulty.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: When clients improve their circumstances, for example, after landing a new, better paying job, Social Services Offices (SSOs) can exercise flexibility to provide extended assistance.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This gives them time to stabilise their finances and strengthens the incentive to gain self-reliance.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: For example, they may take up a Digital Marketing course to move into in-demand job roles, via the new SkillsFuture Career Transition Programme announced at MOE's Committee of Supply (COS).

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Eventually, with employment, they can build their assets through housing and CPF.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We also know some in our society require permanent support.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Together with philanthropy, the generosity of the public and corporates, we have made it possible to care for them as a collective.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This exemplifies our shared ethos of a caring society.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: To ensure its adequacy, we review the ComCare coverage and quantum every two to three years.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: When doing so, we reference data on households' daily living expenses and seek input from experts and community stakeholders.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: While we strengthen our support at the policy level, we must also ensure that Singaporeans in need can access them.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Many low-income families are often time-strapped, having to juggle multiple needs and demands.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We do not want this to become a barrier for them to seek assistance.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This is why we started a major effort to bring assistance closer to families in a more comprehensive, convenient and coordinated manner.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We have also been streamlining processes and facilitating data-sharing.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: For example, we will put together a schemes bundle to strengthen support for ComCare families with school-going children.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Once their ComCare applications are approved, they will not need to submit separate applications to access other support schemes, like MOE Financial Assistance, covered by the bundle.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Through the enhanced SupportGoWhere portal, clients can also apply for ComCare SMTA online, instead of visiting the SSOs in person.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Instead of waiting for clients to turn up at our offices, we want to turn up at their doors, so that we can address issues upstream.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Hence, we have started scaling up Community Link (ComLink) nationwide.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Under ComLink, families with children living in public rental housing will be supported by a team of befrienders.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: They will be the single touchpoint for these families, journeying with them, nudging them towards longer-term goals.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Minister Desmond Lee and Parliamentary Secretary Eric Chua will share more.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Even through the early days of ComLink and working together with the community, we have enabled families to uplift themselves and improve their circumstances.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Singaporeans like Mr Azman and his family are one example.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Mr Azman and his family had been working as delivery personnel to support their two children.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: They lived in a 1-room rental flat and had incurred various arrears.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: With the help of ComLink befrienders and their SSO coordinator, they were encouraged to take small, actionable steps to improve their circumstances.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: They were also supported with ComCare assistance which enabled them to cope with their daily expenses and arrears, while they re-enrolled their son in student care and moved into a larger 2-room flat.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The befrienders and SSO also referred the family to various programmes, enabling them to achieve financial independence in the long term.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Today, Mr Azman no longer requires ComCare assistance and his family is on the path towards home ownership.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We will continue to strengthen the ecosystem of support so that more Singaporeans like Mr Azman and his family can be uplifted.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Because, ultimately, our goal is to enable all Singaporeans to flourish – whatever their race, religion, differently abled or not.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This brings me to my next point on the role of families as a core pillar of our Social Compact.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Chairperson, strong families continue to be the bedrock of our society – a key pillar of strength and our first line of support, complemented by the community and enabled by the Government.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The love and care that family members devote to one another are irreplaceable.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In the face of adversity, our families protect and guide us back onto the right path, like a shining beacon, like a compass, always pointing towards the true north.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Values that we treasure as a society – like love, care and concern, commitment and respect – are cultivated and transmitted through the family.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Strong families also nurture resilient individuals who do well for themselves and their families and who, eventually, we hope, give back to the community.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This is a virtuous cycle that we want to perpetuate and preserve.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Our collective efforts have enabled many Singaporeans to form and raise strong families.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Family remains a core part of Singapore's identity and values.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Findings from MSF's latest "Social Attitudes of Singaporeans" survey show that Singaporean families continue to be close-knit.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The strength of our families was also demonstrated through the pandemic.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Families found new ways to support one another, making extra effort to show their love and concern.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: At the same time, we recognise the pandemic's uneven effects on different families.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Those who were more vulnerable felt the strain more acutely.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: There were also instances of domestic violence and greater mental health concerns, exacerbated by the stressors brought upon by the pandemic.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Furthermore, as Mr Seah Kian Peng highlighted, longer-term challenges lie ahead even as we continue grappling with COVID-19.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Although families have remained strong, the geopolitical uncertainty and changing nature of work are but some examples of new stressors placing a strain on more families.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The Government will journey alongside and support all families in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: First, we will fortify the foundations of all families.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Second, we will strengthen support for families with additional needs.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Members, including Mr Murali Pillai and Ms Ng Ling Ling, have underscored the importance of strengthening our family core upstream.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We must start early by fortifying the foundations of all families.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This begins as early as when a couple commits to getting married.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We must enable couples to build their marriage on a sound foundation with shared values, common understanding and trust.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Marriage is a huge commitment – one of the biggest decisions that most of us will ever make in our lives.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: When two people become joined as one, it can be a big transition.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: There are times when differences arise and may not be resolved easily.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We will partner selected solemnisers to mentor newlywed couples in their first year of marriage.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This complements the suite of marriage preparation and enrichment programmes that help couples prepare for and strengthen their marriages.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We have found early success in a similar programme for the Muslim community called Bersamamu, led by Minister of State Faishal Ibrahim, then in MSF.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: With the foundations of a strong marriage, couples will be more confident and ready for parenthood.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We will also continue supporting couples on their parenting journey, by making Singapore a great place for raising families.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We will enhance the quality, accessibility and affordability of our preschools.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: At the community level, MSF will support the Families for Life movement.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We will integrate our ecosystem of support for families with children, especially across the social-health domains, as I shared at MOH's COS yesterday.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: As Dr Tan Yia Swam mentioned, we must also bolster support for our extended families – they provide an additional layer of comfort.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We recognise that many extended families were unable to gather as often during the pandemic.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The eventual easing of safe management measures (SMMs) and resumption of in-person activities would allow for extended families to gather, while staying safe.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Let us show appreciation for our grandparents, grandaunts and granduncles.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We invite Singaporeans to do so, by joining Families for Life's annual "Celebrating Our Grands" initiative.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We also recognise that every family's journey is unique.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Some face greater challenges and pressures, often beyond their control.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We will do more to enable these families.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Earlier, I spoke about our comprehensive range of support for low-income families.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In addition to those, we have also expanded other national initiatives – like KidSTART and UPLIFT; and enhanced the Fresh Start Scheme.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Coordinated via ComLink, they support low-income families across multiple domains; enabling the Government to adopt a family-centric approach, rather than being agency-driven.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: For families with more complex needs, we provide specialised support.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We will press on with our efforts to tackle family violence.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: They will be implemented over the next few years.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We will continue reviewing social safeguards to ensure they stay relevant whilst balancing the need to divert gamblers from illegal operators which pose significant law and order, and social concerns.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We will also continue working with the National Council on Problem Gambling to promote public awareness of the harms of excessive gambling.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Families with members who are persons with disabilities may also face unique challenges.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We have ramped up support for them over the years through our Enabling Masterplans.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Today, we have a more inclusive education system for students with special needs, enhanced employment support for persons with disabilities and a growing ecosystem of support for caregivers.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Parliamentary Secretary Eric Chua will share more on how the Enabling Masterplan 2030 will achieve an even more inclusive Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We cannot build an inclusive and caring society without everyone getting involved.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In fact, there are many families who are leading by example.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Some foster children, providing a nurturing environment for them to flourish.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Others adopt children in-need, giving them love and stable homes.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We hope more families will be encouraged to step forward to achieve our shared vision of a more caring, just and equal society.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Chairperson, in our work at MSF, beyond families, we join hands with many organisations in the social service sector whichnshare our vision of building a resilient society, underpinned by strong families.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: During my engagements with social service professionals, a common theme that emerged was the need to place the family at the centre of our interventions, to engage collaboratively with the families so that they feel involved and empowered to turn their lives around.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Last year, Big Love worked with a family, where the father had repeatedly hit his children and spouse.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: After ensuring the children's safety, the centre worked with both parents to help them understand how their actions have negatively impacted their children.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: They also taught them to care for their children safely and responsibly.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The centre also built a network of community support around the family, joining hands with NUH, Rotary Family Service Centre and Children's Wishing Well charity.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Through a family-centric, collaborative approach, Big Love was able to help the family address their issues and heal.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: There has been no recurrence of harm since.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The father also spends more time with his children now.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Big Love's success is a testament to the critical role that our partners play on the ground in our endeavour to build strong families.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: I agree with Mr Seah Kian Peng that we must grow the capabilities of our many Social Service Agencies (SSAs), like Big Love, to support them in the good work that they do.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We want to enable them to continue delivering quality, innovative and sustainable services to build strong families and meet growing needs.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We have also seen corporates stepping up to support SSAs during the pandemic.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: For example, Amazon Connect worked with WE CARE Community Services to remote-enable their call centres.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: NCSS and stakeholders from the people, private and public sectors are also working to refresh the Social Service Sector Strategic Thrusts, or 4ST.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The refreshed roadmap will set out the sector's commitment to building more future-directed services and capabilities over the next five years.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: It will also advocate for more strategic partnerships between corporates, SSAs and other community partners.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: More details will be released later this year.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: These sector-wide developments will also benefit our social workers, who are at the heart of our social service sector and our Family Service Centres, or FSCs.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Mr Leon Perera and Mr Louis Ng asked about support for our social workers and FSCs.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: FSCs are resourced based on the number and complexity of active cases.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: FSCs can hire more social workers if caseloads increase and allocate cases based on the workers' experience and complexity of cases.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: FSCs can tap on their accumulated programme reserves to hire additional manpower.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In FY2020, 68% of FSCs had an average of at least 1.5 years of programme reserves.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: MSF works closely with FSC leadership to monitor the caseloads and hiring, and adopt supervision practices that support the welfare of our social workers.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In this manner, MSF balances between being prescriptive and allowing FSCs flexibility and autonomy to respond to needs, while looking after our social workers' interest.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Together with the Government and families, they care for those in need and reinforce the transmission of social values that we treasure, from one generation to the next.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Last year, we celebrated the contributions of Singapore Women to our families and our society.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Building on this momentum, I am pleased to announce that we will dedicate 2022 as the Year of Celebrating SG Families, or YCF.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This movement will be led by Families for Life, with the support of the Government as well as our community and commercial partners.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: First, MSF will engage the public and stakeholders via the Alliance for Action to Strengthen Marriages and Family Relationships and their partners, to explore how we can jointly act to strengthen families.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Second, families can look forward to celebratory events, programmes and useful family resources, with three themes – Celebrating Families; Championing Family-Friendly Workplaces and Culture; and Caring for Families.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We will start with the FamilyTrees planting initiative this Saturday.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Parents can commemorate the birth of their baby by planting a tree – a reminder of the enduring role that families play in our lives.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Families can also look forward to a National Family Week during the June holidays.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Fun-filled events, promotions and family life education programmes will be lined up, including a family carnival; hopefully, with very little SMMs.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: YCF will also see the launch of a new family zone at Gardens by the Bay this July.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We will share more in the coming months.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: (In Malay):   Mdm Chairman, families are the bedrock of our society.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: During difficult and challenging times such as during this pandemic, it is our families that we turn to for support and strength.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: I am thankful that family and family values continue to be treasured by Singaporeans, including the Malay/Muslim community.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: However, families will inevitably, face stressors along the way.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In this regard, the Government has worked with the community to strengthen the family institution.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Three years ago, we started the Bersamamu Programme, for Muslim solemnisers, the Kadi and Naib Kadi, to journey alongside Muslim soon-to-wed couples and newlyweds during their first two years of marriage.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We will continue to strengthen support to all families, especially those who need additional assistance.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We will scale up KidSTART nationwide progressively and enhance support for families with children living in public rental housing through Community Link, or ComLink.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: It is heartening to see families which have done well coming forward to contribute.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: For example, many Malay/Muslim families have become foster parents to children in need.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Seeing them open their hearts, their families and their homes readily to children in need is, indeed, heartwarming and admirable.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: YCF will involve Government agencies, corporates and community partners, including the M3 agencies – namely MUIS, MENDAKI AND MESRA – as well as individuals and M3@Towns.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: There will be a range of celebratory events, programmes and useful family resources to look forward to.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Strong and stable families shape individuals with resilience to strive and succeed.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This is key to propelling the Malay/Muslim community forward.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: I will elaborate more on the support for the Malay/Muslim community in my MCCY speech.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Let us continue to support one another, especially those in need.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Together, I am confident that we can build the best future for ourselves and our families.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: (In English): Singaporeans have weathered many trials together since Independence.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We will be tested with many more trials to come, but our spirit of working together will keep us strong, no matter the challenges ahead.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In our work at MSF, we will continue supporting and uplifting families at every stage of their lives.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: When families are strong, our nation, too, will be able to chart our way forward on a firm foundation for generations to come.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We want all our families and every Singaporean to succeed.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Over the years, we have put in place many programmes and schemes to enable Singaporeans to do well in areas, – such as housing, healthcare, education, employment, skills, social support and more, and provided additional help to those who have less.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Ms Ng Ling Ling asked how MSF will better support such families and Mr Leon Perera also made a few suggestions.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Policies, programmes and partnerships are important, but paradigms and processes are crucial, too.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The way that our ecosystem works together and integrates together to deliver social services matters.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: As Minister Masagos Zulkifli said, we are making a fundamental shift in our paradigm.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We want to be proactive in our approach, put the family at the centre, tap on their strengths and that of the community around them, organise our collective resources around them and try to go as far upstream as we can, so that we provide holistic support that addresses their various needs.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This is a deep shift in how we deliver social services, from a programme- or agency-centric approach, towards a family-centred one.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Through this approach, we seek to empower the family to secure a brighter future – by, first, stabilising their circumstances, then enabling them to grow in self-reliance by building up skills and resources and, ultimately, to achieve social mobility.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Mrs Tan is a working mother with school-going children and she recently lost her job.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Her first step might be to visit Workforce Singapore (WSG), to find work, amongst other organisations.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: But WSG officers do not just help Mrs Tan look for a job or upskilling opportunities.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: And when they realise that she is in financial hardship, they will proactively link her up with a Social Service Office (SSO).

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: That is what we are training our frontline officers to do – to identify the various needs of a client, beyond their presenting issues and connect them with the relevant support.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Going forward, we will extend this training to our community partners and volunteers, so that families can get comprehensive support as soon as possible.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: WSG can link Mrs Tan up with an SSO using Case Connect, our new online platform which we launched last year.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Through Case Connect, agencies can refer cases to one another, share case updates, discuss next steps and bring in more partners if required.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This makes it a lot easier for our colleagues to coordinate with one another and keep track of all case updates to have greater impact.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The SSO then assesses Mrs Tan for ComCare assistance.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: To do this, they can use another digital system – One Client View, or OneCV, which was also launched last year.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: OneCV allows our frontline colleagues to pull the client's relevant information, with the client's consent, from other agencies seamlessly.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For instance, Mrs Tan does not have to submit her CPF statements or her children's birth certificates for her ComCare application.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Instead, she just provides her consent for the SSO to draw the relevant data from Government agencies backend.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We will continue to enhance Case Connect and OneCV and extend them to more organisations progressively.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The SSO assesses that Mrs Tan qualifies for ComCare.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For Mrs Tan, once the SSO officers assess that she qualifies for ComCare, they will also assess whether her children are eligible for Student Care Fee Assistance (SCFA) and MOE financial assistance (FAS).

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: OneCV and SAPs will reduce the number of times that clients have to be interviewed and means-tested.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: They also reduce the administrative load for our frontline colleagues.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: However, in some cases, SAPs still require families to submit separate applications for different schemes, which can be administratively cumbersome.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Since 2018, eligible ComCare clients automatically receive MediFund assistance and bursaries for full-time Polytechnic and ITE students.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We will expand on this effort, to build a "schemes bundle" to support families with school-going children.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Mrs Tan's Primary school-age children are enrolled at an MSF-registered Student Care Centre (SCC).

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: So, they will also automatically qualify for maximum SCFA subsidies for 12 months.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This applies to children with special needs who attend special SCCs, too.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This schemes bundle covers Mrs Tan's children from Primary school to pre-tertiary studies, including after-school care.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: She need not worry about submitting and tracking multiple applications.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We will progressively bundle together more schemes that cover other domains.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Mrs Tan's example illustrates how we are organising support around the needs of families, rather than have them come around our agencies or programmes.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We will continue to make our processes even more convenient for families by digitalising our social services, while ensuring that in-person support remains available for those who prefer face-to-face interactions.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Today, we have the SupportGoWhere portal, which consolidates information across Government schemes into one website for easy reference.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: But users still need to approach the various agencies separately to apply for the schemes.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: So, we will enhance the SupportGoWhere portal so that users can also check their eligibility for different schemes, apply for assistance directly and receive prompt updates on their application on a single platform.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: By the second quarter of 2022, families can apply for ComCare Short-to-Medium-Term Assistance (SMTA) and submit relevant documents through the portal directly instead of having to apply in-person at an SSO.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: They will then receive a phone or video call from SSO officers to understand their situation and assess their application.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For those who prefer to speak to an SSO officer in person, they can still visit the SSO.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We will progressively support more schemes application on this portal.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: These improvements will reduce the burden on families-in-need, allowing them to better focus on longer-term goals.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: These are the ways that we are transforming our delivery of social services, to provide more comprehensive, convenient and coordinated support.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This approach is exemplified by our flagship initiative, which we launched in 2019 – Community Link, or ComLink for short – which several Members spoke about.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: ComLink supports families with children living in public rental housing to achieve three long-term outcomes that we mentioned earlier – stability in meeting basic needs; self-reliance where they can support themselves; and finally, social mobility, so that they can improve their circumstances.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: ComLink embodies the proactive family-centric approach that we are moving towards.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We proactively reach out to families to understand their needs and aspirations.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We draw relevant data across agencies, with the families' consent, to get a 360-degree view of their situation as best as possible.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We work with the family and across agencies to develop goals and a dynamic common action plan.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: And we then bring in customised programmes and services tailored to their needs, with the support of community partners, donors, corporates and volunteers.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Mr Faisal Manap asked how we can build strong relationships with these families.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: My colleague, Parliamentary Secretary Eric Chua, will then elaborate on our progress in scaling up ComLink.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: As I have explained, ComLink goes beyond episodic transactions with families, towards building longer-term relationships with them, partnering them, empowering them to grow.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This is a much more impactful but intensive approach, involving many agencies and partners.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: As we scale up ComLink, we expect to run up against significant fiscal and manpower constraints.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: To find ways to better manage our resources while ensuring greater impact, we have been running learning pilots with some of our ComLink families since last year.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We are streamlining our front-end interactions with the families.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Instead of burdening families with the need to interact with many different agencies and their frontline officers, we assign a pair of befrienders to each family to serve as a constant touchpoint.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: These befrienders journey with the family, celebrating their achievements and encouraging them through setbacks.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Over time, they build rapport and trust, allowing them to better understand the family's unique circumstances and encourage the family towards their goals.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The befrienders share their understanding of the families with the SSO.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We have seen good results from our befriender pilot.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: With befrienders, we can consolidate the manpower needed for public outreach across different agencies and programmes.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Given how closely befrienders work with ComLink families, we agree with Mr Don Wee that befrienders must be trustworthy and adequately trained.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We also have a training roadmap to equip our befrienders with the skills, knowledge and tact to support families.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: As a start, our volunteer befrienders will be paired with MSF colleagues to befriend these families.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This way, we tap on both the expertise of our colleagues and the energies of the community.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Looking ahead, we will strengthen backroom integration across agencies.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Many ComLink families are also supported by other programmes, such as KidSTART for children up to six years old, UPLIFT for Primary and Secondary school students, or M3's Project DIAN for Malay-Muslim families.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Agencies that run these programmes often carry out similar functions.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This will also reduce coordination costs and enable us to provide more integrated support as we gear our systems to look at the progress of families more holistically, instead of along agency- or programme-specific lines.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: To sum up, I have set out the many things that we are doing to transform our social service delivery ecosystem along our new paradigm.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: These are not technical fixes or technical changes.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: These manifest the shift that Minister Masagos Zulkifli talked about in our social service paradigm.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: At the same time, this will also empower our frontline colleagues and social work professionals so that they, too, can focus on the most meaningful part of their mission – to support their clients through their challenges.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: From community and religious groups to corporate partners, many give their time and resources generously to tackle inequality; ComLink and our other efforts to strengthen social service delivery help them achieve greater social impact by better identifying the specific needs of low-income families, through befriending and data integration across agencies; and minimising duplication and wastage across agencies, through stronger coordination of our efforts.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Through asset-based community development and tighter social, health and community collaboration, we focus not only on the needs and gaps that exist in our society, but also the strengths that we can grow, nurture and tap on.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This means building up resources in the community, investing in our families and creating the conditions that enable families to achieve their aspirations.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Let us work together to build a caring and cohesive society, so that all families can be more resilient and benefit from our society of opportunities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Minister Masagos Zulkifli had earlier spoken on the important role that families play in our lives and society and on how we will make Singapore a great place for families.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Families provide the basic ingredients for us to grow into resilient and caring individuals.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: When family relationships are strong, they provide a safety net for individuals and a safe harbour to go home to.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Families can also empower us to contribute meaningfully to society and lead happy and fulfilling lives.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: MSF is committed to providing support to build strong families and strong family relationships.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Today, I will elaborate on three key areas of our efforts to do so.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: First, we celebrate and support families with varying needs throughout all stages of their life journey.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Second, we will continue to build a fairer and more inclusive society where men and women can realise their career and family aspirations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Third, we will continue to invest heavily in early childhood development, so that every child can have a good start in life.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Chairperson, families have played a central role in supporting us through the ups and downs in the past two years of the pandemic.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In the face of COVID-19 measures, we all have found ways to adapt and care for our family members to the best of our abilities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: It is thus timely to celebrate and strengthen the important role that families play in our lives, as Mr Murali Pillai, Ms Ng Ling Ling and Mr Seah Kian Peng have mentioned.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will progressively introduce FFLC to more towns from 2022.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: During YCF, we will scale up family bonding activities and continue to offer family enrichment programmes to equip couples and families with skills to cope with common stressors.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: YCF will also build on the work of the Alliance for Action to Strengthen Marriages and Family Relationships (AFAM), which I chair.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh had asked for an update.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: AFAM was set up last year to co-create and implement solutions with key stakeholders and community groups in six Focal Areas (FAs).

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Allow me to share the preliminary direction for each FA.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: FA1, otherwise known as FAM Connections, led by FFL, will increase awareness and adoption of resources and evidence-based programmes on marriage and parenting.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: FFL will work closely with the Centre for Fathering, Mums for Life, the People's Association and many other ground-up groups.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will also work closely with faith communities via FA6, or Faith and Families, which will organise cross-sharing of experiences and learning points by religious organisations on their efforts to strengthen marriages and family relationships.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For the other focal areas, FA2, Support for Young Couples, will strengthen the delivery and uptake of marriage preparation and enrichment programmes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We also aim to guide newly-weds in considering fertility health issues.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: FA3, or Parenting Together, will engage parents to identify key child-raising challenges, especially as young children grow up in the digital age and face mental well-being challenges.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will encourage more parents to take up evidence-based parenting programmes, such as Triple P and Signpost.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Alongside FA3's work, MSF and MOE will develop resources to empower parents to support their child's mental health and well-being under the Interagency Taskforce on Mental Health and Well-being, which I had touched on during MOE's COS.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Even as we celebrate families this year, we recognise that family relationships are a constant work-in-progress.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Melvin Yong asked about how MSF will support stressed families.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: FA4, Support for Single Parents, and FA5, Support for Families with Early Risks, will work closely with partners to deliver and develop initiatives that support families which may face challenges.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Louis Ng asked about support for single unwed parents.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This is a focus area under FA4, Support for Single Parents.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Our Marriage and Parenthood incentives aim to promote marriage and encourage parenthood within marriage.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This reflects the desired and prevailing societal norm.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: And these include the Baby Bonus Cash Gift, Working Mother's Child Relief and Parenthood Tax Rebate.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Single parents who need additional social support can approach Social Service Offices (SSOs) and Family Service Centres (FSCs) for assistance.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Through FA4, Support for Single Parents, we are working with stakeholders and community partners to understand and address pain points that single parents have.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We had conducted focus group discussions and understand that single parents face challenges with childminding, access to employment opportunities and in some cases, specific cases around housing.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: On childminding, MSF is partnering a Social Service Agency (SSA) to pilot a childminding service outside childcare centres' operating hours.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will share more information on this soon.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: To support upstream efforts to prevent family violence, FA5 will develop initiatives to raise awareness and share information on the building of safe, respectful and healthy relationships.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: FA5 will complement our broader efforts to tackle family violence.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: There has been a steady increase in the number of enquiries and new cases on family violence received by Family Violence Specialist Centres and the Integrated Services for Individual and Family Protection Specialist Centres in recent years.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Various agencies, including MSF, will work with our partners to implement them over the next few years.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For instance, as recommended by the task force, the MSF refreshed the Break the Silence public education campaign in November 2021 to increase awareness of the types of abuse, including non-physical forms of abuse, and to encourage survivors and bystanders to seek help.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Also, in line with the task force's recommendations, we are enhancing our approach to better rehabilitate perpetrators of family violence.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This includes amending the Women's Charter to enable mandatory assessment and treatment orders to be made for perpetrators with mental health conditions that contributed to the risk of family violence.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: While the primary responsibility for complying with rehabilitative Court orders lies with the perpetrator, we recognise the importance of strengthening rehabilitative approaches to encourage perpetrators to complete their rehabilitation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: To provide more intensive and specialised support and rehabilitation for perpetrators, we will also deploy forensic-trained psychologists to community-based family violence specialist agencies by the end of this year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Not all perpetrators require alternative accommodation – perpetrators assessed to have low-risk of recurrent violent behaviours may receive intervention while living in their family home.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Others may prefer staying with other family members or friends.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: To enhance the safety of survivors, we will implement a more structured referral system for social service professionals, so that perpetrators may be provided shelter, if they require accommodation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will study the feasibility of a mandatory structured residential programme for the rehabilitation of high-risk perpetrators.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Chairperson, women have always been key pillars of our families and society.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: While Singaporean women have made considerable progress in the past decades, many still bear a disproportionate amount of family and caregiving responsibilities and may face glass ceilings due to gender stereotypes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Hence, our work to strengthen families must include efforts to support our women.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Seah Kian Peng asked about the initiatives in the White Paper, which sets out concrete action plans to collectively realise our vision of a fairer and more inclusive society.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We have been rolling out some of these plans over the past year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For example, to protect women against violence and harm, we revised the sentencing framework for sexual and hurt offences, with increased penalties for some offences.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We also released the report by the Task Force on Family Violence.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: To address gender stereotypes through education, we refreshed the Character and Citizenship Education curriculum to help our students understand the equity of familial roles and gender stereotypes about careers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Across all domains, we will consider changes to legislation and policies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: But policies must be complemented by whole-of-society action and shifts in mindsets and behaviours.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: More policies and initiatives will be announced when the White Paper is presented to Parliament.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Chairperson, the Government is committed to supporting Singaporean families in their journey to raise their children.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I will next be speaking on MSF's initiatives to give every child a good start in life, regardless of their family background.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We have been steadily building up preschool places.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will develop about 10,000 more full-day places by 2023, to meet the growing demand for preschools.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Ms Joan Pereira will be happy to know that these new preschool places are concentrated in areas with more young families.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For example, in the two newer estates of Sengkang and Punggol, the number of infant and childcare places has increased by nearly 60% in the past five years.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will further lower fee caps at Government-supported preschools in the coming years, so that working families pay around Primary school fees plus after-school student care fees for full-day childcare in the medium term.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We agree with Mr Melvin Yong that the quality of early childhood education is critical to child development.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Hence, we will continue to drive quality improvements in the sector, even as we make preschools more accessible and affordable.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: To better support the professional development of early childhood educators and leaders, we will provide clearer guidance on career and training pathways.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: While early childhood professionals have long been undertaking training, efforts have been uneven across the sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Early childhood educators and leaders are crucial to driving the quality of education and care of our children.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The LDF will guide educators to strengthen competencies in curriculum, pedagogy, as well as strategic and administrative leadership.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will also enhance the Advanced Diploma in Early Childhood Leadership as a milestone course to better develop these competencies in our educators before they are appointed as centre leaders.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: While many preschools already have quality teaching practices, this tool will set a common standard across the sector and guide educators on the use of effective pedagogical practices, identified based on empirical research and ground practice.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will also launch the Early Childhood Learning Communities, starting April this year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: These learning communities will foster peer sharing of pedagogical knowledge and practices among senior educators and curriculum specialists, focusing on domain areas crucial to child development, including Social and Emotional Development, and Language and Literacy.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: To ensure programme quality in preschools, the Government has also developed national curriculum frameworks to guide the development of their programmes and curriculum.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: ECDA will review the Early Years Development Framework for children aged three and below to include areas, such as the learning of Mother Tongue languages.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The revised framework will also provide more detailed guidance to support educators in creating learning experiences to develop important knowledge and skills like socioemotional skills in children.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The refreshed framework will be ready by end-2023.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We recognise that some families face additional challenges and need additional support in developing their children's potential.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The Government is committed to strengthening support for children from low-income families so that we narrow the gap starting from their early years.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In tandem with KidSTART's nationwide scale-up, we will deepen partnerships with corporate and community partners through the Growing Together with KidSTART initiative.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Ms Joan Pereira will be happy to hear that since the initiative began in 2019, we have received over $4 million in cash donations and sponsorships.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Over 1,000 volunteers have stepped forward since 2016 to provide support for KidSTART families, including encouraging eligible families to join KidSTART and helping to pack and deliver essential items to families.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I sincerely thank all our partners and volunteers for their contributions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The Government is also committed to ensuring the adequate provision of early intervention, or EI, services for children with developmental needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: To meet increased demand for subsidised EI services, ECDA will expand the number of places under the Early Intervention Programme for Infants and Children, otherwise known as EIPIC, through the construction of two new EI centres.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: (In Mandarin):   The COVID-19 pandemic has demonstrated the central role that families play in supporting us through the many ups and downs of life.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: As such, it is timely for us to designate 2022 as the Year of Celebrating SG Families to celebrate and support Singaporean families.
