speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Last year, we set up the Alliance for Action to Strengthen Marriages and Family Relationships (AFAM) to work with key stakeholders and community groups to co-create and implement solutions to strengthen marriages and families, including families with young children and those with early risks.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: To provide upstream support to parents of young children, MSF is supporting the Families for Life @ Community initiative by offering more marriage and parenting programmes that are conveniently accessible.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will also press on with our efforts in tackling family violence and will implement the recommendations from the Taskforce on Family Violence over the next few years.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For example, we will make legislative amendments to the Women's Charter to strengthen the protection and support for survivors of family violence as well as rehabilitation for perpetrators.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: On early childhood education, we will further raise the quality of early childhood professionals and programmes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: (In English): Chairman, in closing, it takes a whole-of-society effort to make Singapore a great place for families.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: MSF is committed to journeying with families through all seasons of life, providing nurturing learning environments for their children and paving the way to a fairer and more inclusive society.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will continue to work closely with our partners to do so and invite all Singaporeans to join us in the Year of Celebrating SG Families.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: In a supportive family environment, we can better navigate life's many challenges.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: But some families, including families with persons with disabilities, lower-income families and youths-at-risk face complex stressors and unique challenges.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: It is our responsibility as a society to journey with these families, share their burden and help them regain confidence to pursue their dreams and aspirations.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: I will share concrete steps that MSF is taking with our partners to support these families.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Family members who are caregivers to persons with disabilities often make silent sacrifices and experience caregiver stress.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We recognise these difficulties and have provided greater support to these families over the years.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Ms Denise Phua, Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song and Mr Mark Chay asked about the current support for persons with disabilities and the progress of the Enabling Masterplan.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We have provided greater support in several ways.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We also extended the School-to-Work Transition Programme in January last year and launched the Enabling Mark in October 2020 to recognise inclusive employers, amongst others.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This will allow our DACs to hire more care staff and to increase the quality of care for clients.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We are similarly reviewing the Sheltered Workshop programme.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We have also kept assistive technology devices affordable for persons with disabilities and seniors through the Assistive Technology Fund (ATF) and the Seniors' Mobility and Enabling Fund, which Mr Pritam Singh raised.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Permanent Residents are also eligible for the ATF, with differentiated subsidy rates in line with our position to provide more subsidies to citizens.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: From April 2019 to December 2021, about one out of 60 ATF beneficiaries were PRs who are seniors.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The most common claims included mobility devices like motorised and manual wheelchairs, hearing aids and daily living aids.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We recently increased the ATF subsidy for Singaporeans with per capita household income of between $801 and $2,000 and expanded the range of items that seniors can be subsidised for to include medical devices like oxygen concentrators and suction pumps.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: More can be done to support persons with disabilities.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: I am co-chairing a cross-sector committee with Mr Gan Seow Kee, vice chairperson of the Singapore Business Federation, to develop our next edition of the Enabling Masterplan, or EMP2030.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: EMP2030 will set meaningful longer-term goals to foster a more caring and inclusive Singapore, which will continually be monitored to ensure that we are on track on our objectives.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Today, there is a gap in services for adult persons with disabilities who do not attend any regular disability service after graduating from Special Education schools.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: One of the ways is through piloting regional Enabling Services Hubs (ESH) and Enabling Business Hubs (EBH).

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The Enabling Services Hubs (ESHs), co-funded by the Tote Board, provide persons with disabilities above 18 with a greater range of options for flexible social and learning activities.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Each ESH will identify and reach out to persons with disabilities and their caregivers in their region, understand their needs and link them to relevant support.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Those at risk will be further supported by community befrienders.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: It will also provide on-site services such as continual learning programmes and social inclusion activities, for persons with disabilities and respite care for caregivers.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: While the ESHs serve those with care needs, the EBHs support work-capable persons with disabilities who require customised and longer-term support to work.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We will share more information on these pilots later this year.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Ms Rahayu Mahzam and Ms Yeo Wan Ling raised an important point about doing more as a community to support caregivers.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Last year, NCSS, SG Enable and community partners formed the SG Together Alliance for Action (AfA) for Caregivers of Persons with Disabilities to co-develop a self-sustaining community support model for caregivers.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We started with two pilot sites in Boon Lay and Kampong Glam and the AfA has begun to support the implementation of two projects.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Project 3i is a caregiver-led initiative to provide social and emotional support for caregivers that is integrative, individualised and intentional.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: It will connect caregivers to form community networks and support caregivers through peer mentorship and professional support.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The second project is Community Circles, where a small group of friends, neighbours, or volunteers forms a "circle" of support around caregivers, to provide practical and emotional support.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: These projects have initiated an ecosystem of community and peer support that reaches out to caregivers.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We will evaluate the outcomes from the pilots and facilitate collaborations, so that more networks can be established to support caregivers.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Minister Masagos Zulkifli and Minister Desmond Lee highlighted how MSF has been working to strengthen our social safety net and the delivery of social services so that low-income households requiring assistance can get comprehensive, coordinated and convenient help.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Mr Leon Perera will be happy to know that we have been tackling food security and unhealthy eating as part of this broader effort.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We also provide comprehensive support to households on ComCare schemes, which can include cash assistance for basic living expenses, such as food.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The community also plays a big part in tackling food insecurity.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Many charities and community groups have stepped forward to offer food support – dried rations, cooked meals, grocery vouchers – to families facing food needs.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: As Ms Denise Phua has mentioned, the efforts of these groups have gone a long way in tackling food insecurity in Singapore but there are some overlaps and some gaps in the demand and supply of food support.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This platform allows families and social service agencies to search for food support organisations based on their location and dietary requirements, so that families can receive food which meets their needs.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This allows us to move towards a more data-driven and choice-led food landscape where families can choose their preferred type of food support.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: But we also want to go beyond addressing immediate needs and look at families' longer-term needs.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This is where Community Link, or ComLink, comes in.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Dr Shahira Abdullah asked about ComLink's objectives and our strategy to help families to attain them.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: In the short term, ComLink focuses on helping families with children and youths living in rental housing to achieve stability, where their basic needs, such as day-to-day living expenses and whether their children are attending school regularly, are addressed.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: In the medium term, we support families towards self-reliance, such as to obtain a stable job and to sustain that employment.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Stability and self-reliance then serve as building blocks towards the longer-term goal of social mobility, where the family achieves real income growth and the children and youths are able to achieve better life outcomes.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: ComLink achieves these objectives through its three key pillars.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We then provide targeted and coordinated case support and then journey with each ComLink family to address their issues before they become more deep-seated.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Together with the family, a customised action plan addressing the families' issues step-by-step is assembled.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: A pair of befrienders provide even closer support.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Befrienders journey with families through their ups and downs and help to keep families' sights on their long-term aspirations, dreams and goals.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Together, they work with the SSO coordinators to address issues that each of these families might face.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: For our support to be effective, all stakeholders must work together.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This is where ComLink's third pillar comes in, where the Government brings together different community partners, corporates and volunteers to provide support for families, based on collective knowledge about a community's needs and strengths.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Together, we have introduced some 74 ComLink programmes to date, including enrichment programmes, to provide children with holistic development, sports programmes to engage youths and support groups for parents.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This complements the schemes and services that Government agencies are providing and, through such customised support, we can then have a stab at a transformative effect and set up families for success.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Mr Mohd Fahmi Bin Aliman will be glad to know that we are fully on track to scale up ComLink over the next few years.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We launched ComLink for 11 towns in 2021 and will kickstart efforts for the remaining 10 ComLink towns in the coming months.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We also want to give all our youths the opportunity to succeed in life.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: For those with difficult backgrounds and challenges, it is even more important that we support them.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The family plays a central role in guiding youths down the right path, particularly during adolescence, and being an anchor through the transition into adulthood.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: MSF is committed to helping families to do this better.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We recognise that mental well-being is an important point not just for youths, but for everyone.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: As part of the Interagency Taskforce on Mental Health and Well-being, MSF is working together with various Ministries and agencies across multiple sectors to strengthen mental well-being in Singapore.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We will increase accessibility to a continuum of services across our healthcare institutions, schools and community agencies, so that everyone can receive the appropriate level of care and support.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We also want to make sure that these services are well-integrated, so that it is easier to navigate the mental health ecosystem.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: National Council of Social Service (NCSS) will expand the Beyond The Label campaign to involve more partners and the public in encouraging early help-seeking and greater acceptance of persons with mental health conditions.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: As Minister of State Gan Siow Huang has previously mentioned, NCSS and MOM are studying ways to strengthen support for persons with mental health conditions before and during employment and for their colleagues, so as to create a more inclusive work environment.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: These are all complex issues that can only be solved through a whole-of-society effort.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: As Senior Minister of State Janil Puthucheary has mentioned, the task force will be conducting a public consultation on these ideas and we look forward to developing a national strategy and action plan together with all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Another group of youths who may need special attention are those who leave the formal education system early.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Like Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong and Mr Seah Kian Peng, we believe in the tremendous value of mentoring for these youths.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Under CAMP, mentors are matched with mentees based on the mentees' industries of interest and will guide their mentees in exploring their interests and broadening their exposure to opportunities.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: One of the mentors who have stepped forward is Lawrence Tharekheshwaren Supramany, an ITE alumnus with over 4.5 years of experience in the automotive industry.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: In his youth, Lawrence was involved in a riot.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: However, he turned his life around with the support of his community, notably from his pastor, who provided guidance and tutoring.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Having personally experienced the transformative effect of a mentor in his life, Lawrence intends to inspire other youths as a CAMP mentor.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: MSF will track the outcomes of the CAMP youths, such as placement in education, training or employment and assess the suitability of scaling up CAMP beyond the pilot phase.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: As Ms Denise Phua has mentioned, the Lasting Powers of Attorney (LPA) is an important life planning tool should one lose mental capacity.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: To promote greater awareness of pre-planning tools, such as LPA and Advance Care Planning, MSF and MOH will conduct a joint awareness campaign later this year.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We will also launch the new Office of the Public Guardian (OPG) Online system, which allows citizens to digitally make an LPA in a simple, convenient and secure manner.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The fee waiver for LPA applications will also run right through March 2023.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: To simplify the application process, the Family Justice Courts have enabled applicants to apply for general orders through the Simplified Track on the Integrated Family Application Management System since 2019.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This, typically, covers powers to consent to medical and dental treatment, care arrangements, manage bank or CPF accounts and insurance, set up Special Needs Trust Company accounts, and employment contracts.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: MSF also offers the Assisted Deputyship Application Programme (ADAP) for persons with disabilities who do not have mental capacity and who are enrolled in various Special Education schools, Day Activity Centres and Sheltered Workshops.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: ADAP applicants are provided with mental capacity assessment reports at no cost to the applicant and guidance for applying via the Simplified Track.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The Simplified Track costs $40 in Court filing fees and are usually granted within four to six weeks.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The costs and duration are higher for more complex Court orders, which, typically, involve adults and elderly who lose capacity without making an LPA.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Thus, I urge all Singaporeans to have your LPAs registered, to provide peace of mind to yourselves and to your loved ones.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We will continue to work with community partners to facilitate access to pro-bono or low-cost services.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: (In Mandarin):   Families are the bedrock of our society.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: When our youths face challenges, families will always be a refuge to comfort them.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Families are the source of purpose and strength to guide our youths back to the right path and bounce back.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: With families' love and care, I believe that our youths can grow into resilient individuals, fulfil their potential and, ultimately, contribute back to society.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The mental well-being of our youths is an important priority.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: While parents will always remain a core pillar of support, the Government will continue working closely with our partners to complement family support.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We will transform the YMWBN into a national network to develop whole-of-society partnerships to support the mental well-being of all in Singapore.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Youths who leave formal education early also merit special attention.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: MSF will continue to work with the community to strengthen our families.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Families serve as a beacon of light in our lives.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: It is an inspiring light that pushes us to greater heights.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: It is a guiding light that always leads us back if we ever take the wrong path.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: But it is also a comforting light that provides us with refuge whenever the going gets tough and where we need to look towards to share our joys and anxieties.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Our families also serve as compasses that help us navigate through life.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Families shape our values, beliefs and a sense of purpose.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Through the storms of life, we need only reach into our pockets for our compass to help us all find our true north.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: So, in this Year of Celebrating SG Families, let us all aim to become a bright beacon of light and a trusty compass for our families, just as they are for us.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: First, I thank him for reiterating the importance of strengthening family resilience and his articulation of what family means.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Recently, Minister K Shanmugam made a statement on section 377A of the Penal Code and the changing societal attitudes towards marriage and family.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: So, my first clarification to the Minister is whether he could give us the Ministry's position on this.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: My second clarification relates to single mothers and is addressed to Minister of State Sun Xueling.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: I know she is very passionate and empathetic to the stresses that single mothers face.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: She has explained some of the things that have been done for them.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: And my third and final clarification is relating to ComLink, either Minister Desmond Lee or Parliamentary Secretary Eric Chua could address this.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: We all know the importance of going upstream and the good results that ComLink has achieved so far.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: I note that it has already been rolled out to 11 towns and will be rolled out to 10 more soon.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: My question is, if resource is not a constraint and seeing the good results that have come out so far, I am sure all the 10 towns are looking forward to this.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: So, how can we roll this out even faster and if this could be shared with especially the 10 towns that are expecting this?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: What can we do to accelerate this so that we can really make a difference to the families that will benefit from this?

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: As Minister for Home Affairs and Law Mr K Shanmugam has shared, the Government recognises that section 377A of the Penal Code is a divisive issue.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The Court has acknowledged that the Government's current approach on this matter avoids driving an even deeper wedge in our society.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Our society can be described as largely traditional.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: However, we now have a wider range of views and attitudes where families and marriage are concerned.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: For example, take the attitude towards mixed marriages.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: And you see this more common, even among ourselves and our Members here, very acceptable to our society.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We, therefore, are not surprised that we are seeing an increasing acceptance of LGBT persons socially among Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This was also reflected in statements, consequent to Minister K Shanmugam's statement in Parliament recently, by various parties.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Family continues to be the bedrock of our society and contributes to social stability, allows children to thrive.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We will uphold the traditional family in our Government policies and laws, reflecting our societal norms and values.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: These include marriage, parenthood, adoption, fertility treatment even, housing and inheritance, amongst others.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: At the same time, we must continue to ensure that LGBT persons are protected from violence, harassment and abuse.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: For instance, the Protection from Harassment Act (POHA) contains a range of both civil and criminal measures that can protect all victims and is meant to protect all victims against offences involving harassment and abuse.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: From MSF, through public education campaigns, such as Break the Silence, to raise awareness and encourage victims, regardless of nationality, marital status, gender, race, religion or even sexual orientation, to seek help early.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We also urge the public to step forward to report violence and abuse where LGBT cases may be involved.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Concerns surrounding section 377A and its implication will still have the potential to polarise society.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: It is an issue that involves deeply-held beliefs and values and divergent societal views and goals.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We thank the religious, sectoral, civil society and LGBT groups that have shown support for civil dialogue and respect for the values of others, even when different from their own.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We will continue to adopt the approach of civil dialogue, working with all, involving all stakeholders as we chart our own unique Singapore way forward, without creating sudden shifts and deep divisions in our society.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I have said this before and my views have not changed – I respect single parents, single unwed parents, for the love and care that they have for their children.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: And I fully recognise that it is not easy to bring up children, even more so single-handedly.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: That is why in the Alliance for Action to Strengthen Marriages and Family Relationships (AFAM), we have a dedicated focal area on single parents.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: And this is important because we know that when we solve childminding issues and concerns of single parents, they then will have the capacity, the time and the energies to look into employment.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The third pain point that has been highlighted to us has been around housing.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: In this particular area, I have had the opportunity to work with Member Mr Louis Ng for many years when we have discussed this in Parliament and in my time at the MND.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: These three areas – childminding, employment support, housing – have been brought up as pain points and we are actively looking at how we can solve these pain points for our single unwed parents.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I also wanted to highlight that after the focus group discussion that my team at MSF and I had with the single unwed parents – and Members like Mr Louis Ng and other Members of Parliament had joined me for the session as well – my team had followed up individually with the single unwed parents to clarify any outstanding issues that they had raised, which sometimes also arises out of misunderstandings or miscommunications of Government policies in their interactions with Government agencies.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: I want to thank the Member for his clarification on ComLink and I also want to thank the Member for attributing the adjective "success" with ComLink at this point.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: What we are trying to achieve through ComLink is our promise in our Social Compact: to help our low-income families.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: This is really going for the long haul because if you look at the broad objectives of stability, self-reliance and social mobility we are talking about – and mostly, on social mobility – we are talking about long-term outcomes.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Through ComLink, we are tracking various outcomes, indicators, not just in terms of immediate process indicators, but also perception.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: I want to stress the fact that, actually, time or speed might not be of the essence in this scenario.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Because we are talking about having a very customised, very bespoke approach to going to each family, understanding them, both their challenges that they face, as well as the aspirations and dreams that they have; and then helping them to take away, remove or sidestep some of these challenges while, at the same time, working towards their longer-term goals, their aspirations.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: I do not think it is something that can be achieved overnight.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: You cannot get to Rome in one evening but we can most certainly do that if we adopt a whole-of-society approach – where the community, our social service agencies and the Government come together.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Then, I think we have a fair chance at success for this programme.

speaker: The Chairman
text: So, I am going to ask Members to please ask your questions succinctly and for the replies to also be short.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: I have some questions on the adult disability care.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Is the staff-client ratio of adult disability care facilities lower than that of the teacher-student ratio at SPED schools?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: If so, why is there this disparity between the two?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Because this is what causes the cliff effect for those who are graduating from SPED schools.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: And lastly, does MSF have any plans to close this gap, given that most SPED school graduates will need to attend post-18 disability care facilities?

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: On the first question of whether the staff ratio for the adult disability care facilities is on par with the SPED schools, I do not have the numbers for the staff ratios for SPED schools on hand at the moment.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: So, I cannot give a fair comparison across these two types of facilities.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: On the second point about closing the gaps, I do think that what we are doing is journeying with our persons with disabilities and, as I mentioned earlier, what we have done is to, over time, where necessary, increase funding.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Our intention is really to make sure that we cater for the right amount as well as the right type of services that our persons with disabilities need within the community.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: In terms of closing the gap, that is definitely what we hope to do.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: That is why in the iterations of the three Enabling Masterplan (EMP) since 2007, we have been keeping at it.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: We have been working on the fourth edition.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: I hope that Members can look out for the announcements that we make under EMP 2030.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I really appreciate Parliament Secretary Eric Chua's sincerity in working with us on the ground.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I also appreciate Mr Gerald Giam's concern for persons with disabilities.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: My supplementary question is whether MSF would consider convening a very specific group – either you call it Alliance for Action (AfA) or any action group – that will look into the overall holistic needs of this community.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Because to ask for, say, free transport or free schools is not complete.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: So, the amount for education alone is going to be a lot bigger.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Rather than asking individually, I do think we need a holistic strategic study of the entire needs of the disabled, then prioritise them, cluster them, size it up, see what is needed and then look at how much can be supported by Government grants, how much can be supported by those who can afford a bit more, and those who are in the community – Temasek Foundation or Temasek Trust for that matter, which have been very helpful – and other foundations.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: So, look at it holistically, convene a group that will look at it as a whole, size it, compute how much is required and then see how we can actually operationalise the whole thing for sustainability and to meet the prioritised needs.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Likewise, I want to thank Ms Denise Phua for her passion in this area of work, which I think is really infectious whenever she is at the EMP meetings where she brings with her great ideas as well.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: We will not shun away from our responsibilities on this.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: That is why the Disability Office, Social Policy and Services Group (SPSG) in MSF, is there, and that is why we will continually look at these issues in totality and not just look at them from our own vantage point, but to also look at them together with our partners in the community, the social service agencies.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Which is why, in today's EMP 2030 Steering Committee, we have a whole range of representations from both the people, private and public sectors.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: It is an endpoint, but it is, to me, just a checkpoint.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: It is the fourth, but, definitely, not the last masterplan that we will have.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: We will have to keep working at these issues because some of these things that we want to change in society pertain to mindsets, culture, how we maybe even react to persons with disabilities in our midst.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: So, there is a lot of work for us to do together and I want to give the Member the assurance that we will be keeping at this for the long haul.

speaker: The Chairman
text: I like the passion in the room, but I would like to please remind everyone to be succinct.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: So, would that not be a way to reduce the administrative load of the Ministry and, at the same time, helping to reduce the bandwidth tax on applicants?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The SupportGoWhere portal provides a digital enabler to help families to navigate support schemes and to be able to make the applications digitally.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But we are mindful that many of our clients, including seniors, are more comfortable face-to-face, maybe on the phone, and befrienders will be a big plus.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And so, all that remains – in fact, that remains core – because, in this line of work, in social service delivery, it is high-touch, high-feel.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But a digital platform adds another layer of support.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Even in the real-world space, I have described earlier streamlined action protocols, One Client View (OneCV) and Case Connect working in the backend to enable organisations to work around the client's needs and their families, even as the client approaches the Social Services Office (SSO) physically.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And for clients who approach the SSO, way before COVID-19 or just before COVID-19, we had already put in place video conferencing capacities to enable a client of the SSO to communicate not just with the SSO officer physically but virtually be able to link-up with the HDB officer and, of course, with other agencies as well.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, that remains an important way to support those who may not be so digitally inclined to seek help that way.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I just want to assure Ms Carrie Tan that we do not want a cliff effect and disincentivise someone from graduating.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This is not how we are going to go forward.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Minister Masagos Zulkifli mentioned that, through ComLink, there will be a proactive approach to appear at deserving residents' doorsteps.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: So, I guess the lower-hanging fruits at this moment will be the existing clients in the SSO systems as well as there are also likely to be referrals from the Family Service Centres of ComCare recipients.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: So, my question is, can the potential pool of clients be expanded to beneficiaries of the MOE Financial Assistance Scheme (FAS), MediFund as well as the various self-help groups like SINDA, MENDAKI or CDAC?

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: So, by doing so, their application process must have a housing type and identifier in the application process.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: And it will also mean that system requirements will be required.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Along the same vein, relating to the app which allows clients to apply for various schemes, I guess this is like the Municipal Services Office (MSO) OneService app equivalent for less-privileged Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: So, over time, I hope the app can also allow these clients to apply for schemes offered by the self-help groups and the ComChest accredited Voluntary Welfare Organisations (VWOs).

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I also welcome the various improvements, like OneClientView, the single means-testing approach, as well as the tele-counselling which expedites the application turnaround time.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: So, to improve the handshake process further, can we also explore co-locating SSOs as well as the Family Service Centres, or SSAs, in future because the newer rental precincts do not come with spacious void decks these days.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Lastly, I would also like to thank the —

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: I also want to thank the Member for his three clarifications.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: So, I do not think it is something that we want to take lightly.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: And once we are on a steady state with the existing 14,000 families, we will want to move on to as many other families that we can assist as possible.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: For the second question, the answer is we will take a look at that and we will, gradually, progressively, evolve what we can provide in the technology and in the app.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: We have also co-located SSO and AIC in Bedok and also in Tampines Hub.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: As we evolve the delivery of social services, we can look at how we can actually co-locate some of our services as well.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Please keep it short so that I can let the other two clarifications be asked.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: On the topic of preschool accessibility, I am very glad that Sengkang and Punggol will have more preschool places.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Dawson, which I serve, also has many young families.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: So, I hope and look forward to more preschool centres there.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I hope the Ministry can reach out to them, understand their needs and help them register in a nearby centre with a vacancy, because I know most parents and grandparents will want to put their charges at a centre near their homes.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I also want to make a general point that, for other New Towns or some of the older estates where there are new insertions of BTOs, ECDA will work closely with agencies to quickly expand places through expansion of existing centres, but bearing in mind that there are sometimes manpower constraints and they will also be looking into the development of new centres in additional sites, which will, hopefully, provide convenience to young families which have moved into these new BTOs.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: On the Member's second question, currently, parents may register their interest in a preschool via the Preschool Search Portal, which is an online self-help portal.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: On this portal, parents can actually search by proximity, understand more about which are the centres that are available, what is the waitlist situation like.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Every three months, the portal will inform the parents about the latest situation around the preschool places.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: And if the Member is aware of specific instances whereby the parent is still unable to locate a preschool which is suitable for the family and the child, to please highlight the situation to myself, to ECDA, and we will follow up closely to find a preschool which, hopefully, the parents can accept.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Sometimes, parents can have their specific requirements around specific preschools.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: They may sometimes want a specific preschool within a specific walking distance from home and we will try very much to accommodate.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, on a national level, in terms of preschool capacity, we have enough, but we recognise that, in localised areas, there may be areas with higher demand and, when that happens, ECDA will work closely with the parents and the advisor there to help those young families living in those areas.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: I note that some other countries do publish this data.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: When will the next review be and do these reviews take into consideration new research, such as the study by Prof Teo You Yenn and Dr Ng Kok Hoe that I referred to?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: The Minister referred to our intergenerational social mobility being better than North America and Europe, if I heard him correctly.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Could the Minister reference what is the study that demonstrates that?

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I will try to answer that in three minutes.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: For the UK, it is about 9%; Europe, 11%.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This is published, as I mentioned, by Chetty et al, from the US, UK, Denmark, Canada; the authors are from these countries.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: For the other issue on the publication by the academicians, particularly around what the Member called minimum income standards, this was responded to by MOF in October, giving its views about the minimum income standards.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This was a study started in the United Kingdom in 2006.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: So, it is a relatively new approach in determining what are the benchmarks and standards to look at in alleviating poverty.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: For this particular standard, the idea is to determine what incomes different household types require to reach a socially acceptable living standard.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: It has nothing to do with determining what low-income families should get.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: As such, even the Singapore study reflects the processes and outcomes expected from the study by the UK condition and do not necessarily reflect the needs of the low-income households.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Nonetheless, I will respect that this is an approach, a particular academic approach, and like the UK exercise, it should be seen as a reflection of what society aspires everyone to have for them, like what they want to have at least for themselves.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Nonetheless, there are many other academic approaches to social spending.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: These include those around measuring outcomes on social mobility, like the publication I mentioned just now, as well as issues around social inclusion.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: In Singapore, for example, we make sure social inclusion is something we work very hard on.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Hawker centres are a very good example where the rich and poor dine together under a community hall and they do not feel rich, do not feel poor.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: In the same way too, community clubs, even our housing estates, are designed for that.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: There are other studies which talk about how it should be done.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: For example, raising average incomes, building pathways for continuous improvement.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: These two studies that I have mentioned by the academics —

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Put emphasis on personal responsibility, the role of the family and not just Government intervention.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: So, I hope that we do not get fixated by a publication, as popular as it is, but look at the broad literature and the outcomes that we have achieved so far.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Seah Kian Peng, if you can withdraw your amendment, please?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Chairman, I would first like to thank Minister Masagos Zulkifli, Minister Desmond Lee, Minister of State Sun Xueling and Parliamentary Secretary Eric Chua for their responses to our cuts and also their subsequent responses to our clarifications.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Renewing and strengthening our social compact to build a fair and just Singapore require the work and support of all of us.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Certainly, for those in the social sector, I think they are doing a lot of heavy lifting on this front.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: So, on behalf of all of us, inside and outside of this House, I want to express our sincere appreciation to all of them.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: On that note, I beg leave to withdraw my amendment.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Chairman, I have for several years now supported the broad principle that the family unit is the foundation of Singapore society.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: At the same time, I made the call for a wider definition of what a family unit comprise.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Such definitions are not mere semantics – they carry with them moral and policy weight – for the Government encourages strong families by way of subsidies, programmes and support.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: In turn, such families are themselves sources of support for its individual members.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Therefore, if I may make a pragmatic point, lightening the load on the state and the tax burden on society.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: It is thus an important point to consider – what is "family" in Singapore today?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Here, I would say, we can be even more inclusive.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: All these trends have put stresses on the institution of family across different life stages.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Mental health, which we discussed just now during the COS on MOH, is such a big issue now.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: These stresses also add to the negative impact on Singaporeans' well-being and Singapore as a society.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: The late Dr Ong Chit Chung, then Member of Parliament for Bukit Batok, argued in this House, that the family should be called the "pillar of society" instead.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: For "if the pillar is eroded or weakened, society will not stand".

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: As we pitched battle against COVID-19, the Singaporean family was a pillar of strength holding us together.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: To date, we have about 850,000 infections, more than 1,000 have died.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Our families, as the first line of support, lovingly cared for the sick.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: When any succumbed, we cried as a family and rallied around each other.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: When our children were not able to attend school, our families encouraged them in their remote learning from home and took care of their mental health.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: When in doubt or fear, we found strength in talking to each other, to get vaccinated, boosted, wear masks and commiserate about the need for safe management measures.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Families helped those who have lost jobs or suffered pay cuts.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: The time-honoured qualities of our Singaporean families which includes resilience, self-reliance and filial piety must be preserved.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I believe, ultimately, it is the strength of our families that will determine whether our nation will emerge from this pandemic stronger.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: A lot can be done at the community level to celebrate family milestones and share ideas as to how to keep families strong.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: In Bukit Batok, we regularly hold birthday celebrations for our centenarians.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: There is no better celebration than to see up to five generations of family members coming together.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: One centenarian whom I met was Mdm Ng Ah Luah who lived until 105.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I asked her for advice as to how to keep a family harmonious.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: She told me she would organise frequent family gatherings to bond over food.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: She also said, family members should not bicker over little things.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Simple lessons but difficult to put in practice.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: We must provide more support for families that face challenges in keeping together.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Today, more than ever, it is needed as a pillar for our society facing so many challenges, for if it is eroded or weakened, society will not stand.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: (In Mandarin):   Mr Chairman, the saying goes "it takes a village to raise a child".

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: The importance of the extended family has shown itself more obviously in these past two years.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: In general, many married couples live with their children and pay regular visits to both sets of grandparents.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: In the past two years, to prevent the virus from spreading, the Government has imposed various restrictions including the size of family gatherings.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: I believe the majority of families have been compliant.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Less family gatherings, less face-to-face contact; phone calls and video conferences have become the norm of communication.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Most of the elderly I know are not comfortable with a video call.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Uncles, aunts and cousins all form part of the extended family.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: With the current restrictions of groups of five, there is hardly any chance for two families to meet in public.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: They miss their children and grandchildren, but do not want to disturb their work.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: They lose muscle tone, get hunchbacked, unsteady on their feet and tire more easily.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Young working parents face the pressures of job, childcare and elderly care.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: If one has elderly parents who need medical attention, whether in clinic or admission, the barriers to visit are another source of distress.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Because of COVID-19, mask-wearing has become a daily necessity.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: The young are growing up amongst masked faces.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: There is some scientific evidence showing that this could lead to delayed social developments in young children.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Just like how the COVID-19 protocols get streamlined into three, we can simplify rules for interactions and allow people to make their own risk assessments.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Allow families to unite once the COVID-19 situation improves, please.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Mr Chairman, the Government has consistently upheld the philosophy of family as the first line of support as our social compact in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The World Values Survey conducted in 2020 has shown that family remains a key priority for most Singaporeans, forming the core of our social values today.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Upholding the institution of family and keeping families strong will thus be a continuous endeavour that we must be committed to.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I am heartened to know that the number of marriages in 2021 has returned to pre-pandemic levels, despite a slight decline in our birth rate.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: However, there are still some risks that threaten our family institutions as a nation.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Some of the emerging social trends warrant our attention to ensure that we continue to support our Singaporean families to stay strong.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: There are several observations that I noted from the Singapore’s Census 2020 that I would like to highlight.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Furthermore, the COVID-19 pandemic has also taken its toll on some family relationships.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Various studies across the world on the impact of COVID-19 on family resilience have shown that the pandemic has caused psychological distress for children and parents.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In Singapore, our families are also not spared from these effects.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Mr Chairman, in my previous cut on Keeping Singapore Families Strong, I mentioned the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the resilience of family relationships.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In times of strained relationships or when the families are under stress, it is challenging for the family to act as the first line of support.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: During my Meet-the-People Sessions, I often encounter residents who would share with me their family problems.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: A resident couple’s story left an impression on me as it presented the need for greater upstream support when families are faced with early signs of stress.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The couple initially approached me when they were struggling with their finances after their employment was affected by the pandemic.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: They had pressing needs because they had just welcomed their newborn child, but their income dropped drastically at the same time.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In order to take care of the child, the wife decided not to look for employment and the husband became the sole breadwinner, continuing the financial strains of the family.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The couple later developed relationship strains and the husband moved out and contemplated divorce.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This further left the wife in limbo, as she had to fend for financial support and caregiving while going through a difficult time with her husband.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: All this while, I appreciate the partnership and support rendered by the Social Service Office who worked with me and the family to stabilise their circumstances, to help the wife find suitable employment and caregiving arrangements and for the couple to work on their strained relationship.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: As families face financial issues or other unexpected circumstances like health problems, family relationships are bound to be affected.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: They will present early signs of stress, which may lead to greater challenges down the road.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: At a recent dialogue session, single unwed parents spoke courageously about the stigma they faced.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As Minister of State Sun Xueling shared after the dialogue: "They shared the pain and hurt felt when faced with the stigma that comes along with being a single unwed parent".

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We should help end the discrimination and stigma they face.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Our policies should reflect what we already say: “Single unwed parents are valued citizens and, like all parents, are respected for the love and care they provide for their children.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: They are no less a mother or a father, just because their child was born outside of marriage”.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: They are no less a mother or father.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It may be because the cash component is part of the marriage and parenthood package, the key word being "marriage".

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But single unwed parents already receive the CDA component of the marriage and parenthood package.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Why give one and discriminate when it comes to the other?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: For many, it is not a luxury but a lifeline.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Increased costs will hit single unweds even earning $600 a month even harder.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I have raised this many times in this House.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I hope we can finally help end the stigma single unweds face and help provide them with this cash component of the Baby Bonus.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Being a single parent is twice the work, the stress and the tears, but also double the hugs, the love and the pride.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It is twice the work as single parents have to juggle work while caring for their child.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: They do not have an additional pair of hands.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In my Adjournment Motion, I shared the story of Ema, a single unwed parent who raised her daughter in a shelter.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Thanks to HDB and a change in our policies, Ema can now provide a stable living environment for her daughter in a rental flat.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: She now also has a good job but has difficulties keeping her job as she has to work at odd hours on short notice.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: She has difficulties finding help on such short notice on an ad hoc basis.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: She does not have family members she can count on.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Government provide this additional pair of helping hands so single unweds can remain in the workforce, contribute to Singapore and work towards becoming more independent?

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Although the lady is under both Self-Exclusion and Family Exclusion Orders, she has continued to spend thousands of dollars gambling at Singapore Pools using her salary and borrowing from licensed and unlicensed moneylenders.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: However, I believe that we need to consider how to disincentivise gambling and reduce opportunities for gamblers to indulge in their habit.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: I propose creating an additional requirement for Singapore Pools' counter staff to scan the identity card of individuals placing Toto and 4D bets above a certain threshold.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: The purpose of the scan would be to verify that the said individual is not, in fact, under an Exclusion Order and should thus be prohibited from placing bets with Singapore Pools.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: While this will create some delays in the process, I believe it is worthwhile if it deters those on Exclusion Orders from gambling excessively via legal platforms.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Mr Chairman, the COVID-19 pandemic has put a strain on the relationship of many families over the past two years.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Prolonged telecommuting work arrangements, home-based learning and, more recently, a spike in Omicron cases among young children are just some examples of how families can be stretched emotionally, physically and mentally.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Unfortunately, this is felt most keenly by vulnerable and stressed families.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: What is the Ministry doing to support families upstream to address stresses early?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Can we do more to support couples from the point of marriage?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Can the Ministry provide an update on the progress in implementing the recommendations by the Taskforce on Family Violence, which were released just last year?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: We should do all we can to support families and strengthen family bonds.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Seah Kian Peng, please take both your cuts together.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: First, more equal workplace opportunities; second, more caregiver support; and third, increased protection for women.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: I know we are all now looking forward to the White Paper which I am sure will draw from these conversations.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Can Minister share about some of the initiatives which might be in the White Paper?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Can the Minister also share some data and statistics on the size and the type of problems that Singapore women face?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Even as the Government puts in place new policies and laws, I would also like to ask if there are specific areas of improvement we must bear in mind relating to our mindsets and attitudes.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: For example, in the light of the recent attention on sexual misconduct towards women, I note that most Institutes of Higher Learning now have compulsory respect and consent courses.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: But shifting mindsets must not just be within a section of society but it must involve everyone.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Second, this bias is not just a matter of serious misconduct, but of everyday behaviour.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Interruptions, patronising explanations and unwarranted assumptions of emotional fragility – I think all these are poor companions to our social life.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: But these are experienced by many women on a daily basis.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: What can we all do to promote this mindset shift?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: All children deserve to grow up in loving families.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Adoption is certainly a complex process as, even with the best of intentions, there are many minefields to navigate.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: And the people who are affected, they include the children being adopted, the adoptive parents, adoption agencies, agencies supporting foster parents, the pregnant mother, lawyers and so on.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Some poor behaviour must clearly be constrained, for example, any suspicion of "marketing" children as if they are goods for sale, rather than human beings to be nurtured and loved.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Some parents, for example, are tricked into giving up their flesh and blood to strangers.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: On the other hand, there are those people who are unfit to be parents but, yet, refuse to give consent for their children to be adopted.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Whether they have abandoned the child or cannot be found, or have neglected or ill-treated the child, one has to ask if the consent of these adults, who, in my view, are not fit to be parents, is required.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: There is a case to be made that such parents have no standing as parents.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: In any case, can the Ministry provide updates on the progress of the review?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Can the Minister also provide some background on the state of adoption in Singapore?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Can the Minister let us know where Singapore lags behind the rest of the world and what can be done in these aspects and how we can do better?

speaker: The Chairman
text: Ms Joan Pereira, please take both your cuts together.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Chairman, to build a Singapore that is "made for families", we have to make it more conducive for our busy parents, many of whom are working full-time and long hours.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Parents have shared with me that getting a place in a preschool within walking distance of their homes has been particularly challenging.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Parents normally place their child's name or children's names on waiting lists and the wait can be several months or even longer, causing great anxiety for parents.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The early years are especially important for children's development.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: We must seize this golden window of opportunity to nurture and help them build a strong foundation for learning.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: However, some families from disadvantaged backgrounds face various challenges in sending their children to preschool.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: In my division, KidSTART is effective because ECDA and community partners work very closely together to tackle issues in a more comprehensive manner to better support families in need.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I speak to all the agencies and they concur.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: However, I hope the Ministry can share with us regularly how our families are progressing with all these interventions in place.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Do they need more help or are there gaps that need to be plugged?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Sometimes, such help can be more effectively and quickly provided by the community itself.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: How many more children are expected to be included?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Will community partnerships be considered so as to widen the scope of programmes that can benefit the children and their families?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Mr Chairman, Sir, students from low-income families tend to be more vulnerable to long-term absenteeism in schools.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Such programmes, like the widely praised Bolsa Famílias, have have been found to improve school attendance and even cognitive development internationally.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: This is not a novel concept in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: An independent study of its impact found positive feedback from parents and students.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Its recipients maintain regular attendance, perform better in school, were more engaged and more confident in achieving educational goals.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Whilst specific aid programmes, such as the MOE Financial Assistance Scheme (FAS), are useful in fulfilling specific educational needs, they typically have strict conditions on the usage of the aid.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Conditional cash transfers are nudges that, nevertheless, enable families to retain the freedom to choose how best to fulfil their needs, be it for better nutrition or savings for University education.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: The Straits Times School Pocket Money Fund study found that some recipients were keen to save the money.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: I was most heartened to read that as it could help them build healthy financial habits to cope with future difficulties.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Some may object that such a policy creates moral hazard and some families may get their children to be absent to get the grant.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: There are levers to guard against this by keeping the grant small and directing it only at lower-income or multi-problem families.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: Mr Chairman, quality preschool education is vital in allowing our children to achieve their fullest potential in life.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: How often does the Early Childhood Development Agency (ECDA) review the pedagogies of our early childhood curriculum?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: What are the areas that ECDA will focus on in the coming years to further improve the quality of our early childhood education?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: Beyond curriculum, can MSF share what are its efforts to build the key competencies of our preschool teachers?
