speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: Has there been an increase in attrition among local preschool teachers?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: One teacher told me she is tired, but yet, she cannot afford to be sick because there would be no one left to help cover her class.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: Can ECDA ensure that there are sufficient teachers in our preschools to cope with the increased workload?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: The quality of our preschools depends heavily on the quality and quantity of our childhood educators.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: For our future generations, we must do more to make early childhood education a choice profession.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Mr Chairman, given the marked rise in cost of living in recent times, is MSF bringing forward the review of the quantum to be given to eligible recipients of the ComCare and Public Assistance schemes?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Also – and perhaps this is a radical idea – does the Minister think that the current criteria are sufficient, or is there a case for us to explain the giving of public assistance to more people?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Public assistance is given to the poorest amongst us and it is a long-term assistance scheme, in contrast to short- and medium-term care.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Public assistance is bare bones – it is for those who cannot work as a result of old age or illness and have little or no family support.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Parents with children receive help in educational expenses.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Many of these are elderly men who are not married.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: First, is the number of 4,000-plus on public assistance too few or too many?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Is there a case, for example, to be made that our qualifying criteria are too stringent?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Second, is $600 too much or too little?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Can the Minister give an idea of how this $600 was derived and whether it ought to be reviewed in light of recent inflationary pressures?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: I know our philosophy is to give adequate, but not generous, welfare.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Certainly, for the most part, I agree with this because a bloated welfare state with a high tax burden is something that Singaporeans collectively do not want.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Still, as a society and a government, let us think more deeply about what is required for this group in our midst – how they could live a dignified life and with peace of mind.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Of course, in addition to $600, there are many other forms of help and many other partners in the community who do give help.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: But $600 a month, I think in the present circumstances, is a precarious way of living.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Can we do more to help this group of the poorest amongst us?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: Mr Chairman, Sir, in my Budget speech, I argued for a war on poverty and a different approach based on defining a poverty line, channelling all schemes through FSC social workers, reducing the stress involved in applying for financial assistance, providing longer lead times and larger amounts of financial assistance based on new research and with part of it tied to conditions.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: I also called for more aggressive early intervention for children born into poor families.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: The overarching goal should be to achieve a massive measurable dent in poverty and the poverty cycle.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: I am specifically calling for FSCs to be able to approve and administer all the various state financial assistance schemes directly for those defined as poor and at risk.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: I argue for FSCs to be like venture capitalists, making financial investments, coaching and hand-holding to get a return on that investment.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: Social workers today do not actually administer the aid in all cases.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: My arguments on the financial aid application process and amounts are also separate issues from what ComLink per se is focused on.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: To do all this, social workers need visibility on the holistic situation of the family.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: Vulnerable families often face complex issues, such as chronic illnesses, mental health issues, school absenteeism and other social issues.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: Hence, more needs to be done to ensure that social workers get that visibility via tools like One Client View and other forms of cross-agency data sharing, with permissions.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: Social workers should see an increase in their remuneration, given the increased scope of work.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: Social workers are professionals battling a national crisis on the frontlines and should be adequately compensated.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: A revolving door of social workers is detrimental to the support offered to vulnerable families.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: Above all, efforts should be made to expand recruitment so as to lower caseloads, as I spoke about in my Budget speech.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: And lastly, Sir, one possible objection to all I have thus far said is this: one could say that providing more welfare support to the poor more smoothly will breed welfare dependency.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: By doing this, we will trap the poor in a cycle of welfare dependency and will doom them and their children to poverty.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: We used to hear this argument a lot.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: We still do and it is heard around the world.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: Such arguments are not without a grain of truth.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: I am not calling for unlimited welfare aid that is so much that it discourages work.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: Above all – I am just wrapping up – we must set ambitious goals to massively reduce poverty and the poverty cycle.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: A nation which does not set ambitious goals in any policy arena —

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Perera, I am afraid you have to end.

speaker: The Chairman
text: You are almost a minute over your time.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: I understand that under ComLink, the Social Service Office (SSO) for each town leads a team consisting of Government agencies, corporates and community partners.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: I note, Sir, that a good interpersonal relationship between the beneficiary and the case worker is a pertinent factor behind the success of such programmes.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: In this regard, I would like to better understand ComLink and request that MSF provide details on how beneficiaries are engaged and managed.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: For example, is each family assigned with one case worker?

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: Is there any minimum number of engagement session requirement for each family in a month?

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: And can MSF also share the ratio of beneficiary to a case worker?

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: On a related note, Sir, I believe it is also important that the beneficiary is fully involved and committed.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: However, many low-income workers are engaged in jobs that involve irregular hours, such as daily- or hourly-rated work or food delivery.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: Also, time spent on programmes, interviews and counselling is time not spent working.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: I propose providing such individuals with a make-up allowance so as not to deter them from participating in such programmes towards their long-term benefit.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: With this programme, low-income families will be matched to dedicated befrienders and get customised help to address their problems as well as help families connect to community groups and Government agencies so they get more targeted help.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: I am excited about these developments as I feel that it will help to render more timely and holistic care for the families with young children.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: It does, however, seem very resource-intensive and I have some queries regarding the execution of the programme.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: How do we ensure the competencies of the befrienders?

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: How do we match them to lower-income families?

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: Do we have an ecosystem to support them as they approach the different Government agencies?

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: What might be some indicators of success, both short and longer term, that MSF and ComLink partners are potentially looking at achieving?

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: What might be some obstacles to achieving these goals?

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: What is MSF’s strategy in attaining its objectives?

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: Chairman, last year, MSF announced that it would scale up the ComLink initiative nationwide to 21 towns over the next two years.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: I applaud MSF for the efforts to upscale the ComLink initiative.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: Upscaling this initiative would make ComLink towns more accessible to lower-income families.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: Moreover, the expansion of ComLink will also go a long way in supporting low-income families adversely impacted by the pandemic.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: More families can take active steps towards stability, self-reliance and social mobility with adequate social support.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Chairman, MSF piloted ComLink three years ago in 2019 and I am very glad to hear that the Ministry will scale up the scheme over the next two years island-wide.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I want to thank the Ministry for implementing ComLink in towns like Choa Chu Kang.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: This will really help the vulnerable families with young children staying in rental flats.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: At the heart of ComLink are volunteer Befrienders, who play a critical role of befriending and suggesting plausible options for the families under ComLink and journey along with them.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: What is MSF doing to ensure that the volunteer Befrienders are adequately trained and of sound moral character, given he or she will be working closely with different members in the ComLink family?

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: As part of ComLink, would MSF consider implementing a seamless application process for these families?

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: For example, for disadvantaged children who require financial assistance to attend schools, Social Service Offices’ records about their families can be shared with MOE and the schools, so that the children do not need to apply for the Financial Assistance Scheme, the Straits Times School Pocket Money Fund and other related help schemes separately.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Likewise, for other assistance that the families will need, I hope that MSF can tap upon information technology to make all the application processes easier.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: A seamless and integrated assistance application process will need more proactive and closer collaboration amongst all the involved Ministries, including MSF, MND, MOH and so on.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: The COVID-19 pandemic has exacerbated this, with many low-income families struggling from the financial fallout.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: The Community Shop was launched by Food from the Heart and lets beneficiaries choose some groceries every month for free from special minimarts in their area.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: This caters to different needs of beneficiary households, such as those who cook and do not cook, those with children or elderly who may require certain foods.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: Participants appreciate the flexibility and freedom of choice.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: I also propose an electronic point-of-sale system with digital currency loaded in a card.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: A large proportion of the credits could be earmarked for healthier food products to encourage healthy eating.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: The card could also be used at participating hawker stalls for those who do not cook.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: This repeats two calls in my recent Adjournment Motions on preventive health and hawkers.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: NGO Food Bank Singapore has piloted a similar Tap-A-Meal initiative, where beneficiaries are given cards loaded with credit to order what they wish from Encik Tan's menu.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: Chairman, families in need usually struggle with multi-faceted, interlocking problems.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: It takes the teamwork of different Ministries, agencies and volunteers to help them.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: I want to take this opportunity to recognise the efforts of my grassroots volunteers, community partners and Government agencies helping the vulnerable families in my division.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: A coordinator will keep track of the help rendered by the different agencies, share regularly how the family is doing after the various interventions and highlight areas where more or new help is required.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: The families in need also spend a considerable amount of time filling up and submitting multiple forms to apply for assistance schemes under the different Government agencies.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: Will the Ministry monitor these families in the longer term to ensure that they can continue to cope and do well?

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Unfortunately, there are still many residents in need who are either over-served or completely missed out.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: And the impact of giving and volunteerism is not as strong as it should be.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Although MSF attempts to coordinate ground efforts, there is often repeat giving, wastage, food items that are not healthy or do not meet the needs of the beneficiaries.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: In local caregiver support on the ground, there is either lack of a local network, a local plan or a one-stop hub where a caregiver can approach.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: How can the Ministry play a more active role to involve the ground better and also direct help to where it is needed?

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Set up a Local Co-ordinator Network, much like the ComLink network, for young families in need.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: And like ComLink, this network can comprise the local Social Service Office, Family Service Centres, other social service agencies and even the CDCs.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: It can identify, curate, cluster and collate unmet needs; start with the rental estates.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Publish and publicise the needs in a user-friendly and accessible way.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Set up a calendar of giving and volunteering in each neighbourhood.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Educate potential donors on meaningful giving; focusing on needs, allow choice and not trying to create demands.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: And also equip recipient organisations with better volunteer management skills and tools, that are appropriate to their size and bandwidth.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: As a Member of Parliament, it is not uncommon for me to see distraught residents whose loved ones have lost their mental capacity.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: These residents are legally unable to make decisions for the personal welfare or assets of their loved one because a Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA) had not been made before.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Many of them are shocked that they have to apply to be legally appointed as deputies to then make decisions for loved ones who had lost capacity.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: If LPAs are not as widespread as desired, deputyships are even lesser known.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Another group for whom deputyship is relevant are persons who are born disabled and do not have capacity to make decisions on their own.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: They require a deputy when their parents or guardians can no longer make decisions on their behalf, after the age of 21.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: The reasons for this low take-up rate are several: a genuine lack of awareness, difficulty with applications, costs and so forth.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: There is also a need for knowledgeable medical practitioners who have the experience or ability to write a good enough medical report for deputyship applications.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Charities which try to help their clients with disabilities are also crying for help.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: They are not set up or resourced to facilitate deputyship applications for their clients.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: One charity head told me about the shortage of in-house psychologists and the challenges of coordinating with legal professionals.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Will MSF work with MinLaw to start a workgroup to seriously look into: (a) starting a mobile team which can focus on these services for residents and charities; (b) curating a list of experienced medical doctors and lawyers to help them; let fair fees be charged and subsidise applications for the lower-income; (c) developing an effective communication kit readily accessible to residents of different language abilities, education and backgrounds; and (d) training and sustaining a pool of volunteers able to share and guide the applicants.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: To ensure that this plan truly delivers better outcomes for persons with disabilities and the sector, we need to better organise, instil more rigour and constantly review for better results.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I suggest the following steps to be taken at the systemic level.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: One, size the problem and do a better job at communicating all these main clusters of needs to all stakeholders.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Two, assess and cluster the needs according to importance, urgency, size of impact, or difficulty of implementation and pay special heed to areas which are highly important, highly urgent, with higher impact on the population; especially obvious pain points highlighted so many times over the years – the dearth of services for adults; the helplessness of caregivers who continue to fret about what happens to their children after they are gone.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Some who cannot cope basically take their own lives or their children's lives or worry to their graves.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Three, strategically assign task forces to areas of priority.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Give the job to people and organisations with track records, who are not only commentators but willing and able to dirty their hands, tap on their networks and influence or empty their pockets to deliver the results expected of the tasks.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: This EMP4 is not a feel-good exercise to increase the number of volunteers, which is important, but is not first objective, which is to solve the root issues.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: MOH and MND have several that we can tap on.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Partners such as the Tote Board, Temasek and other foundations should be persuaded to address important pain points.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Other stakeholders such as families, family caregivers and advocates can organise ourselves better to fundraise, to find regular income streams, to call upon our networks to resource the disability services better!

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Tough as it may be though, we must never give up this space.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: What new assistive devices has the Ministry noted a high demand for and that were not covered under the previous regime?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Separately, which top five items does it project to have high subsidy utilisation up to 2030 under both SMF and ATF?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: In 2019, the Minister for Social and Family Development shared that 2,037 persons with disabilities had benefited from ATF, a steady increase from 2016 and 2017.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Since then, over the last three years, how many individuals have sought assistance at each subsidy tier?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: The new items covered under the enhanced scheme have not been fully stated in the January announcement.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: There are common examples, but I ask that MSF consider the release of the full range of items that are eligible for subsidised purchase under the new scheme for better public utilisation of both funds.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: There does not seem to be any publicly available information on the dollar amount of subsidies provided to Singaporeans and PRs respectively under ATF before the latest update to the scheme.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Would the Ministry be able to provide a breakdown between Singaporeans and PRs from SMF and ATF utilisation, in dollar terms, since each fund was launched?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Many residents with moderate to severe disabilities require care provided by adult disability care facilities, like day activity centres, adult disability homes, adult disability hostels and sheltered workshops.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Based on publicly available information, I understand the waiting times, depending on centres, can vary from three months to two years?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: If there is insufficient capacity and inadequate staffing at these facilities, this can create a cliff effect for those with special needs.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: They would have been receiving care from special education schools, but have difficulty finding the same level of support after leaving school.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Such funding can help expand the capacity of care facilities and reduce their long waiting list.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: It can also go towards hiring and retaining more good staff, including Singaporeans with better pay and working conditions.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: All this will help enable the centres to conduct more meaningful and effective engagement and training activities for their clients and lighten the worries of their caregivers.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Besides improving the welfare of their clients, it will also give their caregivers much needed respite and allow them to be economically active if they choose to.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: This will produce both tangible and intangible benefits and returns for families, our society and our economy.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: In particular, the topic of future care planning with caregivers weighs very heavily on my heart.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: I take particular note of households with special needs adults in my block and home visits with my residents and I am always left in admiration of our family caregivers' unwavering dedication to their charges.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Some caregivers dedicate their entire lives, foregoing careers and other relationships in order to fulfil their caregiving responsibilities.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: And I think more needs to be done to support them.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: I met Mdm Tan, not her real name, on a block and I immediately was taken by how well-designed her home was.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Her home was specifically designed to allow her brother to live comfortably and happily.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: She used to work in an office but as her brother started to age, she gave up her work and became a freelance interior designer so that she can work from home to care for her brother full-time.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: She is older than her brother by a few years and is worried about his well-being should she not be around to care for him any longer.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: To Mdm Tan, this fear of leaving behind her brother is very real and – given that she is in her late 50s – very near.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: This visit left me with many questions as to how we as a nation and community can help and support the people in the same situation as Mdm Tan and her brother.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Will Mdm Tan's brother be able to age-in-place in a home that he loves should she no longer be able to care for him?

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Is living in a purpose-built facility the only other alternative?

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: What are the interventions out there available for undiagnosed adults with special needs?

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Besides setting up trusts, what other supporting structures do we need to put in place as a nation to support our differently abled countrymen?

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: While these remain as questions to many, to Mdm Tan and many caregivers in her shoes, these are very real, everyday realities with a looming timeline that is ticking away.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
text: Martina Navratilova once said disability is a matter of perception.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
text: If you can do just one thing well, you are needed by somebody.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
text: Persons with disabilities (PWDs) are part of our society and should be given a fair shot and employment without discrimination.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
text: As Members of this House know, I am privileged to be coaching a champion paralympic swimmer Swimming and representing her country have been Pin Xiu's dream.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
text: However, not all persons with disabilities are as fortunate as Pin Xiu.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
text: Through my journey in parasports, I have met many other differently abled individuals.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
text: Some are already in the workforce; some are in school.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
text: But what is most evident is their desire to be independent and productive members of society.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
text: This is why I will be speaking on stronger employment support for PWDs.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
text: This is especially so in Singapore, differently abled or not, but if opportunities are thwarted and with no support by society, there will be no means for survival.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
text: PWDs can work and earn a decent living.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
text: Most PWDs are highly skilled and should be given a chance at employment and not be rejected.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
text: I recognise that over the years, MSF has steadily increased employment support for PWDs.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
text: While PWDs who are able to work have access to job opportunities, there is still more that we can do on this front.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
text: There is also feedback that more services could be provided for PWDs above 18 years of age who are unable to work.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: "Walk with me for a while, my friend; you in my shoes, I in yours.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I thought that is an apt quote to start with, to invite you to imagine walking in the shoes of caregivers of persons with special needs.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I have shared my personal story in this House but it is the stories of others that inspire me to urge for more understanding and more support for these families.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: There are physical disabilities, intellectual disabilities, developmental delays and even within each category, there are different needs.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Some may be high functioning; some require a lot more support.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I would therefore caution against brushing "support" in this sector, with a broad stroke, lest we miss out specific needs and think that we have done enough.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I accept though that it would be unrealistic to expect the Government to provide solutions to all issues and address every problem.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: But there is a need for the Government to synchronise efforts especially on larger issues like early intervention, costs of medical care, infrastructure and also create platforms for people to come together to augment Government support.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Parents among us would understand that raising children can be an adventure.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: We love our children very much but there are days which test our resilience.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Imagine a day in a life of a parent of a child with physical disabilities.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Just washing up your child is a whole logistical affair.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Sometimes, your child runs around in a public place and you need to discipline her.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Imagine a parent of a child with autism, having a meltdown in the MRT.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Calming the child down takes skill and a thick skin, as others watch you, sometimes with judgement or pity.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Thirdly, for these caregivers, the intense anxiety never ends as various challenges emerge and evolve at different milestones of the lives of the persons they care for.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: When they are young, caregivers worry about early intervention, finding the right school, how waiting times to enrol will impact their child and cost of therapies which they hope can help the child's development.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: When the child transits to a different education level, caregivers worry about how he or she would adjust.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: When they grow older and sometimes even stronger than the caregivers, parents worry about their waning strength in handling the child or how anyone else would do it.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: They worry about employment or how their children would survive when they pass on.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: It is against this backdrop that I am asking for some attention to be given to the plans in supporting the caregivers.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: This is, indeed, a meaningful platform focusing on key concerns of the special needs community.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I hope we remain cognisant of the varying needs and deepen our understanding of effective support that can be provided.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: This is work-in-progress and I trust the Government will remain committed to develop the support structures.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I hope the larger community too, will continue to deepen their understanding about different abilities and do their part to embrace and support the caregivers.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: Youths today face a multitude of challenges; in particular, youths who leave school prematurely, after which, it leaves them in a vulnerable state, where they no longer have access to guidance and an environment that can provide them with the right conditions to realise their fullest potential.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: I believe that every youth should be given more opportunities throughout life.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: Many success stories would have credited their success to a teacher, a mentor, someone who along their journey was able to guide them to better understand themselves and amplify their strengths.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: We want all to have such opportunities in life.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Mr Chairman, we know that our adolescent years are a big influence in our lives.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: They certainly shape who we are and can have a profound impact on our outlook in life and our life trajectory.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Those young people who do go into further education after they turn 18 will find many mentors within their education journey.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Those who enter into the workforce, however, may find it harder to do so.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Still, others may not realise the powerful role that mentors play in living a successful life.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Mentors help us develop in ways that go beyond the obvious, beyond grades and promotions, beyond financial and social success.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Mentors are guides in the journey of life and they are especially useful to young people.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Having been a mentor myself, I know that I may not be able to help people avoid mistakes in life and, in fact, some lessons cannot be learnt except through paying for "tuition" in mistakes.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: I can forewarn them, I can forearm them and I can also help in the recovery.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: How many young people have benefited from it and what are some of the variables being measured?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: How do the mentors get into the programme and are there any sorting mechanisms for such mentors who, after all, may be paired with young people who themselves are vulnerable?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Are there any lessons or concerns from such programmes?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Do we have plans to expand the programme, especially to those young people who have not had access to formal mentors in school?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Can I ask that the Minister update especially on the opportunity for lower-income youths or youths at risks, to acquire mentors and the impact that these have on them?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: I shared in my Budget speech that Family Service Centres (FSCs) social workers are asking for a cap on the number of active cases they handle, funding for headcounts and resources for research work, more funding for headcounts and resources for community work.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: I met many passionate social workers, but they struggle with heavy caseloads and were burnt out.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: One social worker told me to tell everyone here, "just tell everyone we are just very tired and frustrated".

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: MSF has programmes for FSCs and monitors and helps them when needed.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: FSCs are also handling more cases which are getting more complex.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Let us help social workers help the most vulnerable in our society.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Mr Chairman, the community, including social service agencies (SSAs), community groups and corporates, all play a critical role alongside the Government in supporting the social needs of Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Indeed, it is the community that has allowed Singapore to pursue a unique welfare model where the state is small, but the work it does is amplified through the effort of community partners.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: During this COVID-19 period, many SSAs, they had pivoted to digital modes and transformed their service delivery.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: For many, this has been an opportunity to reap efficiency gains and to magnify their impact.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Technology has enabled us to do more than we have done before, to reach more people in the comfort of their own homes and at times, most convenient to them.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: It has allowed more frequent check-ins and more innovative use of scarce manpower in the social service industry.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: And yet, SSAs are one of the most high-touch sectors.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: That is to say, the human connection must be established through real meetings, where we can see and we can hear, not just what is conveyed through the camera and microphone, but in a million ways through body language, the blink of an eye, the crossing of a defensive knee, the discomfort unspoken but to an experienced social worker, as clear as a shout.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: In short, with digital modes, the gains are clear, but what we lose are less.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: How will the Ministry help SSAs to be prepared for the future?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Can the Minister let us know how SSAs have harnessed technology and how it measures service delivery?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Have there been any adjustments that social service professionals have had to make and what has been the feedback from clients?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: And finally, have we seen an increase in participation and support of corporates in this space?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Is there more that the Government can do to encourage community partners to step up?

speaker: The Chairman
text: Minister Masagos Zulkifli, would you like to report progress?
